Join the City of Chattanooga Team Chattanooga , a vibrant and growing community of over 190,000 residents within a metropolitan area of nearly 600,000 is known as the "Scenic City" for a reason. Nestled along the Tennessee River and surrounded by the foothills of the Appalachian Mountains, we are a hub of outdoor adventure and innovation. Home to the University of Tennessee at Chattanooga (UTC) and Chattanooga State Community College , our city blends a rich industrial history with a tech-forward future—famously powered by the nation’s first community-wide "Gig" fiber-optic network.​ The City of Chattanooga was also recently designated as a "National Park City,” the first of its kind in the United States. Our Organization As a City, we are powered by a dedicated workforce of approximately ​ 2,600 employees committed to excellence in public service and making Chattanooga the best community in the country. Our team ensures our city thrives through a wide range of municipal services, including: Public Safety: Chattanooga Police and Fire Departments. Infrastructure Utilities: Public Works, Waste Resources, and specialized Stormwater management. Quality of Life: Award-winning Parks and Outdoors and Community Development systems and the Chattanooga Public Library. Transportation: The Chattanooga Metropolitan Airport (CHA) and citywide transit and pedestrian friendly initiatives. Innovation: Leading-edge smart-city programs with a commitment to cutting edge workforce development policies to ensure all our residents can get ahead. Why Choose Chattanooga? The City of Chattanooga’s workforce is the heartbeat of our community. We don't just offer jobs; we offer careers with purpose: making Chattanooga the best city in America. We are committed to being the premier employer of choice in Southeast Tennessee by providing: Competitive Compensation: Robust pay scales that reflect our commitment to our staff. Work-Life Balance: Generous paid time off and flexible scheduling where possible. Exceptional Wellness: Comprehensive health benefits and wellness programs designed for you and your family that deliver savings to you beyond your paycheck, featuring a centralized health clinic and pharmacy for all City employees. . Growth: A focus on professional development and upward mobility within the organization. ​The Great Outdoors: Your Backyard Playground: Chattanooga isn't just near nature, it's immersed in it. As one of the most biodiverse cities in North America, the "Scenic City" offers an ecological richness that few places on earth can claim. Whether you are an adrenaline junkie or a weekend wanderer, world-class adventure is always less than an hour away. ​Vertical Adventures: Scale legendary sandstone cliffs in what is widely considered the premier rock climbing hub of the Southeast. Water Rapids: From the high-octane whitewater kayaking of the Ocoee River to world-class bass fishing and peaceful paddling on the Tennessee River. Trails for Miles: Explore a massive network of mountain biking and hiking trails that wind through lush ridges, hidden waterfalls, and deep river gorges. In Chattanooga, "work-life balance" means you can finish your shift and be at a trailhead or on the water before the sun sets. Our mission is to work together to build a safe, vibrant, and sustainable city for all Chattanoogans. To do that, it takes a team of skilled and passionate individuals. Proficiently performs the duties and responsibilities typically assigned to an Industrial Mechanic Assistant. Demonstrates efficiency and safety in the performance of job duties and usage of equipment. Monitors mechanical systems to ensure proper functioning and to diagnose potential problems; troubleshoots and repairs machinery related to wastewater treatment plant operations. Diagnoses and repairs lift station pumps, motors, sump pumps, valves, and gate valves; performs minor fabrication of parts and pump pulling as required. Diagnoses and repairs mechanical machinery as master pump stations, including pumps, motors, gear reducers, valves, and rake bar systems. Inspects and repairs digester building and related equipment, including positive displacement pumps, gas burners, automatic gas drain valves, boiler systems, and odor control systems. Disassembles and rebuilds centrifuges, including removing and replacing bearings, seals, and ceramic wear rings; performs preventative maintenance on residential grinder pump stations. Examples of experience include machinery and equipment maintenance in an industrial, wastewater or water plant setting. LICENSING AND CERTIFICATIONS: A valid Driver’s License. Must be able to obtain a Forklift Certification. KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS: Knowledge of safe work practices; mechanical and electrical equipment principles; basic plumbing principles; maintenance requirements for plant mechanical and electrical systems; automated equipment operation and maintenance; welding principles and practices; applicable tools and equipment utilized in the trade; and, heavy equipment operation principles. Skill in diagnosing and repairing mechanical plant systems, equipment, and machinery; implementing preventative maintenance on applicable systems, equipment, and machinery; utilizing tools and equipment of the trade; adhering to safe work practices; reading and interpreting blueprints, schematics, plans, technical manuals, and specifications; operating welding and fabricating parts; and, communication and interpersonal skills as applied to interaction with coworkers, supervisor, the general public, etc. sufficient to exchange or convey information and to receive work direction. Incumbents may be subjected to moving mechanical parts, electrical currents, vibrations, fumes, odors, dusts, gasses, poor ventilation, chemicals, oils, extreme temperatures, inadequate lighting, work space restrictions, infectious diseases, heights, and confined spaces. Nestled along the Tennessee River and surrounded by the foothills of the Appalachian Mountains, we are a hub of outdoor adventure and innovation. Today we're sharing another look at CPD's newly launched Drone First Responder (DFR) pilot program. In case you missed it, our DFR pilot program includes two prepositioned drones located at CFD Fire Stations 4 & 9. When needed, officers in our Real Time Intelligence Center (RTIC) can launch these drones and stream live footage to the operators and responding officers.  Why DFR? 1. The drones can arrive quickly and provide first responders with intel to make faster, more informed decisions. 2. They can help improve resource deployment. 3. Perhaps most importantly, they can enhance the safety of first responders and the public. Other things to know about DFR 1. These drones are NOT used for routine patrol or surveillance. 2. This pilot program was fully funded by grant money. 3. You can see details about every flight, including maps, duration, and call types at the DFR dashboard on https://hubs.la/Q04vqVRj0.

Chattanooga Police Department’s Drone First Responder Pilot Program Takes Off CPD announced today the launch of its Drone First Responder (DFR) Pilot Program, designed to provide officers and other first responders with real-time information about active incidents and other emergency calls for service. The program is intended to help officers make faster, more informed decisions, improve resource deployment, and enhance overall public safety.  The program consists of two prepositioned unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) located at Chattanooga Fire Department Stations 4 and 9. These locations were selected based on data identifying areas where violent crime most frequently occurred.  When a call for service occurs, the UAS is launched by a police officer located in the CPD Real Time Intelligence Center (RTIC) and flies to the scene of the call. Once on scene, the drone transmits live video to responding officers, operators, and incident commanders. The drones are not used for routine patrols or general surveillance. CPD’s Unmanned Aircraft System policy prohibits the department and its officers from using drones for general surveillance, harassing individuals or groups, or conducting business not law enforcement-generated or affiliated. Every deployment is governed by federal regulations, department policy, and publicly reported.   An online dashboard provides information on CPD’s DFR pilot program including flight maps, duration, call types, and date/time. This can be found on the Drone First Responder page on https://hubs.la/Q04vp-D80. Data obtained by the UAS shall be retained in accordance with CPD policies: OPS-63, Digital Recording Systems and SOP-22, Digital Evidence. The DFR drones and associated equipment are manufactured by BRINC, an American technology company specializing in drones and software for public safety and emergency response. Officer training and DFR test flights began in late April and the pilot program is now fully operational. #CPDNews

Tennessee has lost one of its greatest treasures. Dolly Parton’s legacy reaches far beyond the music that made her an icon. Her generosity, compassion, and love for the people of Tennessee have touched countless lives from putting books in the hands of children through the Imagination Library to stepping up time and again when her neighbors and communities needed help. Traffic Fatality - 7100 Shallowford Rd. CHATTANOOGA, Tenn. -- The Chattanooga Police Department (CPD) Traffic/DUI Unit was informed by the Hamilton County Medical Examiner's Office that a driver from an August 17, 2026 crash died from the injuries she sustained. The two-vehicle crash occurred near 7100 Shallowford Road within the intersection of the Interstate 75 exit ramp.  Through investigation, interview, and observation CPD's Traffic/DUI investigators determined Vehicle 1 (Ford Edge) was exiting I-75 Northbound when, for unknown reasons, it drove through a red light and collided with Vehicle 2 (Toyota Avalon).  Hamilton County EMS transported the driver of Vehicle 1 to a local hospital. The driver of Vehicle 2 sustained minor injuries and was not taken to a hospital. CPD was notified that the driver of Vehicle 1, a 73-year-old woman, succumbed to her injuries on August 22, 2026.  #CPDNews

Incumbent(s) may not be required to perform all duties listed and may be required to perform additional, position-specific duties.) Supervises, directs, and evaluates assigned staff, processing employee concerns and problems, directing work, counseling, disciplining, and completing employee performance appraisals. Collaborates with Management, Administration, and/or the City Training Coordinator to develop training related to areas of responsibility. Coordinates daily work activities; organizes, prioritizes, and assigns work; monitors status of work in progress and inspects completed work; consults with assigned staff, assists with complex/problem situations, and provides technical expertise. Ensures adherence to established safety procedures, including adherence to OSHA and MUTCD safety regulations; monitors work environment and use of safety equipment to ensure safety of employees and other individuals; ensures setup of safe work zones; initiates any actions necessary to correct deviations or violations. Ensures compliance with Federal, State, and City landscape, forestry, green infrastructure permits, requirements, laws, and regulations. Coordinates work activities with those of other departments, contractors, outside agencies, or others as needed; responds to the needs/requests of other city departments. Develops long-term goals and projects; drafts plans, blueprints, and specifications for proposed improvements; reviews project design and coordinates with the planner on capital projects. Plans and coordinates projects; prepares or receives work order requests; calculates the cost and effort necessary for job completion; prioritizes, schedules, and assigns projects to crews according to available time and resources; coordinates the availability of needed equipment, personnel, and materials; inspects work sites to ensure proper completion of projects, including replacement of landscaping. Develops long-term maintenance schedules; performs preventive maintenance inspections. Oversees operation and maintenance of department equipment; provides training and instruction on proper use and repair of equipment. Monitors inventory of department equipment, supplies, and parts; ensures availability of adequate materials to conduct work activities; initiates requisitions for new/replacement materials; reviews equipment specifications; receives/inspects incoming deliveries; coordinates organization and restocking of stock. Supervises and performs general cleaning/maintenance work necessary to keep vehicles, equipment, and tools in operable condition, which may include inspecting equipment, checking/replacing fluids, greasing equipment, replacing parts, washing/cleaning equipment, or cleaning shop/work areas; monitors equipment operations to maintain efficiency and safety; reports faulty equipment; evaluates and coordinates needed equipment repairs. Supervises and performs the technical and complex duties required during the installation/repair of sewer/storm water pipes and structures; includes the ordering and staging of material, equipment necessary to perform such work; ensures all OSHA guidelines are adhered to in relation to trenching, sloping, benching, classifying, and testing soil types. Supervises, performs, and trains employees in maintenance and construction activities to maintain proper care and functionality of green infrastructure and ornamental horticulture systems; leads and assists in the selection, care, planting, and maintenance of City trees, shrubs, flowers, turfgrasses, other plants, soil, and sod in local parks and other public areas. Selects and recommends flowers and plants for replacement. Identifies common species of plant pests and weeds and utilizes the method of integrated pest management for control. Prepares fertilization, integrated pest management, and irrigation schedules. Applies pesticides, herbicides, and fertilizers, complying with state and federal guidelines, and keeps a record of applications. Performs administrative tasks; receives/approves timesheets and leave requests; prepares payroll sheets and forwards to payroll staff; reports accidents or injuries; reconciles billing for vehicle repairs; maintains television and grouting log sheets. Maintains and updates current blueprints, construction plans, street maps, sewer system maps or other documentation; provides sketches of field information for incorporation into city maps; maintains and updates video library. Prepares or completes various forms, reports, correspondence, lists, logs, work requests, daily activity reports, monthly progress reports, personnel documentation, chain of custody forms, overflow forms, shipping forms, vehicle repair forms, vehicle maintenance sheets, accident reports, property damage reports, inventory records, purchase requisitions, payroll sheets, performance evaluations, diagrams, maps, drawings and other documents. Receives various forms, reports, correspondence, logs, work orders, specifications, maps, drawings, wiring diagrams, mechanical diagrams, vehicle repair forms, inventory records, job applications, time sheets, leave slips, manuals, catalogs, reference materials, or other documentation; reviews, processes, forwards, or retains as appropriate. Why are we choo-choosing to remain focused on bringing passenger rail back to the area? Because it has the possibility to push us forward in so many ways.  We recently took a trip to Raleigh, NC to see how the North Carolina Department of Transportation has been successful with their railways in collaboration with Amtrak. What we experienced was the affirmation that this is an investment worthwhile — from creating $20+ billion in annual statewide economic output to creating 88,000 in jobs supported by rail.  Where does Chattanooga fit into the equation? The Sunbelt Atlantic Railway Coalition has officially been registered as a 501c3, an important milestone to connect Chattanooga to Atlanta, Nashville, and Memphis. MODIFIED BRUSH AND BULK COLLECTION IS UNDERWAY TO HELP SPEED UP COLLECTION.  Here's how you can help!! When setting out your brush and bulky waste for pickup, please keep these essential Do’s and Don’ts in mind so our crews can collect everything quickly and efficiently! We have added more trucks and crews are running 10-hour days, six days a week.  ✅ DO Separate Your Piles Keep yard waste/brush and bulky items (furniture, appliances, etc.) in distinct, separate piles along the curb. Different specialized trucks are dispatched for each material type, so mixed piles can delay pickup! ❌ DON’T Block Piles with Vehicles Park vehicles clear of all waste piles. Collection trucks need ample room and overhead clearance for boom arms to pick up materials safely. ❌ DON’T Place Piles in the Street Keep all waste behind the curb on your lawn or easement. Piles spilled into the roadway create safety hazards for traffic and block storm drains. Brush can be dropped off at the Wood Recycle Center and Bulk trash can go to any city refuse center, both free of charge.  Thank you for doing your part to keep our neighborhood looking great!  #CommunityNotice #WasteManagement #BrushCollection #CleanNeighborhoods #CityServices

When we choose a location for a new tree, we focus on neighborhoods that experience higher temperatures and have less access to shade. Our goal is to bring the benefits trees provide to the places that need them most. Once we identify the right place to plant, we decide on the right tree. While we do provide ongoing care for our trees, we also want to make sure the species we select has what it needs to thrive. Many of our trees face extreme heat, weed eaters, wind, and much more. We do our best to choose diverse, native species that are well-suited to their environment and give them the best chance of survival. School is officially in full swing for Hamilton County students! Drivers, please remember to slow down and stay alert, especially around school buses and bus stops. Passing a stopped school bus when the red lights are flashing and the stop arm is extended is against the law. Drivers in both directions are required to stop, except when the roadway is divided by a physical median, such as a concrete barrier or grass divider. Violating this law in Tennessee can lead to a fine and add 8 points to your driver's license

Domestic violence doesn’t always leave bruises—but it can still be deadly. 😔 In No Visible Bruises, Rachel Louise Snyder pulls back the curtain on how abuse is often misunderstood, minimized, or missed entirely—by friends, communities, and even the systems meant to protect people. Through survivor stories and reporting with advocates and law enforcement, she shows how warning signs can hide in plain sight and why leaving isn’t a simple “just walk away” moment. The book also points to real, practical ways prevention and intervention can work—when we stop relying on myths and start taking patterns, risk, and safety seriously. 💜 What’s one myth about domestic violence you’ve heard that you wish people would unlearn—and why? 🗣️  🔗 https://zpr.io/Lh74aZA482mQ #NoVisibleBruises #EndDomesticViolence #DomesticViolenceAwareness #SurvivorVoices #DVBookClub

After years of service protecting the Chattanooga community, the Chattanooga Police Department (CPD) is honoring the retirement of two members of its K9 Unit: K9 Burt, a decorated patrol and narcotics detection dog, and K9 Duke, who ultimately found his true calling outside of police work. K9 Burt, an 11-year-old Belgian Malinois, retired after 10 years of distinguished service with the CPD. As a narcotics detection canine, Burt was responsible for locating more than $3 million in illegal narcotics and currency during his career. Among his most significant contributions were three separate cases in which he located more than 1,000 fentanyl pills. “K9 Burt exemplified the courage and reliability that every handler hopes for in a partner,” said MPO Luke Timmons, Burt’s handler. “What makes me most proud is that no officers were ever injured by suspects during any of Burt’s deployments.” Having a single handler for an entire working career is a rarity among police K9s, making the partnership between Burt and Timmons even stronger.  Burt also earned recognition beyond Chattanooga for his exceptional performance in training and competition. He was named the United States Police Canine Association (USPCA) Regional Top Dog in both narcotics detection and dual-purpose certifications. During the USPCA Detector Dog Challenge, Burt earned first place honors in the room-search portion of the competition before an untimely bathroom break during the vehicle-search event derailed his chances at the overall title - even elite, highly trained police dogs go when they have to go. While K9 Duke’s career followed a different, less illustrious path, he will be remembered as part of the Chattanooga Police Department family. Despite many months of extensive training sessions, Duke consistently demonstrated that police work was not of interest to him. Ultimately, the K9 Unit retired Duke early and found him a loving home. Duke was originally purchased using grant funding, and all grant requirements were satisfied before his early retirement. The Chattanooga Police Department thanks both K9 Burt and K9 Duke for their time with the department and recognizes the commitment of the handlers, families, and community members who support the K9 Unit. The Chattanooga Police Department wishes both K9s a long, healthy retirement.

Did you know our team has cleared over 40 downed trees since the beginning of May? Extreme weather conditions can weaken our trees, often leading to them coming down. When precipitation varies widely from extremely dry to extremely wet, this stresses out the tree. Dry conditions cause the tree to prioritize the usage of water often leading them to drop large branches, while wet conditions can weaken the tree's roots, causing the tree to fall altogether. No matter how healthy you may think your tree is, exposure to extreme weather conditions can damage the tree in a short amount of time. Always monitor your large trees for signs of degrading health. Check for things like soil cracking around the base of the tree, exposed roots, and prolonged “soupy” soil conditions. Call local arborists for professional advice on the health of your trees.  In the meantime, plant new trees! Don’t wait until you have one come down to plant another. Trees take years to grow and provide the shade that we admire them for. Late fall and winter are the best times to plant trees. This dormant period means the tree can invest all of its energy into its roots rather than diverting energy to leaf and fruit production. Check out the Chattanooga Tree Project to volunteer at tree plantings this winter and be on the lookout for free tree giveaways around the city.

What is not represented in these statistics:  💧 Gallons of water drank  🌞 Amount of sunblock used  🙅 Cans of bug spray gone through  The crew showed up every day, optimistic and ready to work. Meet the dynamic duo of Rasheem McCray and Jerry Gil!  They tackled a job that bike enthusiast will love because it will allow the easy transport of bicycles up and down steep staircases with ease.  After a request from a resident, they promptly installed the narrow metal channels, often called bike runnels or ramps.  Instead of hauling your bike over your shoulder, you just pop the wheels into the groove and roll it up or down effortlessly.  The resident could not believe how fast the team tackled the task.  Great job Rasheem and Jerry!
